title: Using it sensibly: passwords, updates and common scams

videos.script: The last lesson of this course is the one whose mistakes cost the most, and almost none of it is technical. {{cost}} Nobody loses an account because the encryption was broken. They lose it because the same password was used somewhere that was breached, or because somebody was in a hurry and clicked on a message that arrived at the right moment. {{how}} So: what a password is actually for, and why length beats punctuation. The second factor, and which kind is worth the trouble. Updates, which are the cheapest defence there is and the one everybody postpones. {{three}} Then the shape of a scam — urgency, authority, and a channel you did not choose — which is the same shape whether it arrives as a message, a call or a page. {{shape}} And the part nobody plans: what to do in the hour after it has already happened, in the order that actually helps.
